Vegetarian Beef Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Modified: Sep 30, 2026. Published: Sep 30, 2026 by Lindsay Moe.

Vegetarian beef stuffed sweet potatoes are a satisfying main dish that delivers on flavor and is easy to make! It uses two of my favorite recipes, big batch vegetarian ground beef and cashew dressing, to make a simple stuffed sweet potato.

Stuffed sweet potatoes are a vegetarian and vegan staple, and for good reason.

They're easy to customize, but you might not want to after you try it this way! We're cutting the sweet potatoes in half and roasting them cut side down so they get nice and caramelized, then topping them with homemade vegetarian ground beef, cheddar cheese, sweet onions, diced avocado, and cashew dressing.

This recipe is naturally gluten free and easy to make vegan. It's loaded with vitamins, healthy fats, protein, and fiber, so you'll stay full and feel satisfied.

Ingredients

  • Sweet potatoes
  • Olive oil
  • Coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • Onion
  • Garlic
  • Cheddar cheese
  • Vegetarian ground beef crumbles
  • Avocado
  • Cashew dressing

How to make vegetarian beef stuffed sweet potatoes

  1. Preheat the oven to 400ºF.
  2. Rub the cut side of the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place cut side down on the prepared baking sheet and bake.
  3. Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and season with salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to medium low and cook, stirring frequently, until soft and golden.
  4. Add the garlic to the pan with the onions and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant.
  5. To assemble the stuffed sweet potatoes, flip the sweet potatoes over so they are cut side up. Use a fork to mash the inside of the sweet potatoes a little bit, then fill each one with ¼ cup vegetarian beef and ¼ cup shredded cheddar cheese. Evenly divide the onions and avocados over the top and drizzle with cashew dressing. Garnish with minced parsley if desired.

Top tips

Make your own homemade vegetarian ground beef

This recipe uses my favorite vegetarian ground beef substitute. It's a recipe I've used to make hamburgers, salads, and tacos. My kids have a hard time telling the difference between this and real meat, and aren't the least bit mad about it.

I suggest making my big batch vegetarian ground beef recipe so you can just grab it from the freezer to help make this a quick and easy meal. I've included the time it takes to make the "beef" in the recipe card, but if you already have it on hand this recipe is ready in about an hour.

How to know when sweet potatoes are done

Cooking times will vary depending on how big your sweet potatoes are. You'll know they're done when you can easily pierce them with a fork and the cut side is golden brown.

Timing

Depending on what you have on hand, this recipe could take some time to put together, or it could come together very quickly. Consider making my big batch vegetarian ground beef so you'll always have it on hand to throw into recipes like this. However, if you're making it fresh just for this recipe you can let the sweet potatoes roast at 375ºF while the "beef" cooks in the oven to save time.

You could also consider cooking your sweet potatoes the day before, or using leftover baked sweet potatoes you already have on hand. If you're roasting the sweet potatoes night of, let your onions cook low and slow for most of that time so they become silky and caramelized.

How to store stuffed sweet potatoes

You can keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. I recommend adding the avocado fresh when serving instead of storing it cut to prevent browning. You can store the other components separately or fully stuffed.

You could also freeze everything except the avocado and the cashew dressing for up to 3 months. Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and warm in a 400ºF oven until warmed through, then top with the avocado and dressing.

Tips for customizing stuffed sweet potatoes

  • Leave off the cheese (or use a vegan version) and use a flax egg for your "beef" to make these vegan stuffed sweet potatoes
  • Add 8 ounces of sliced mushrooms with the onions
  • Add leftover roasted vegetables or oven roasted broccoli
  • Swap the cashew dressing for your other favorite homemade or store bought sauce or dressing (bbq sauce would be great!)
  • Swap the homemade vegetarian ground beef substitute for your favorite store bought vegetarian ground beef crumbles
  • Meat eaters can substitute cooked ground beef

FAQ

Can I use a regular baked sweet potato?

Yes, you could bake whole sweet potatoes and stuff those with the filling. I like the caramelized edges and quick cooking time of cutting them in half. I got this idea from Pinch of Yum's sweet potato stacks.

What is cashew dressing?

Cashew dressing is a creamy vegetarian homemade sauce that tastes great on just about anything. It's made with cashew butter to keep it simple and quick to throw together.

Recipe

Vegetarian Beef Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Baked sweet potatoes stuffed with homemade vegetarian ground beef crumbles, melty cheese, onions, and avocado, then topped with creamy cashew dressing.
No ratings yet
Print Pin Rate SaveSaved!
Prep Time: 10 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 1 hour hour
Vegetarian ground beef: 1 hour hour
Total Time: 2 hours hours 10 minutes minutes
Servings: 6
Calories: 577kcal
Author: Lindsay Moe
Prevent your screen from going dark

Ingredients

  • 3 sweet potatoes, halved lengthwise
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • Coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 large onion, thinly sliced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1.5 cups shredded cheddar cheese
  • 1.5 cups vegetarian ground beef crumbles, warmed, see notes
  • 2 avocados, cubed
  • Cashew dressing, to taste, see notes
  • Minced parsley, for garnish, optional

Instructions

  • Preheat the oven to 400ºF. Line a large baking sheet with aluminum foil.
  • Rub the cut side of the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place cut side down on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 60 minutes or until the sweet potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork and are caramelized on the bottom.
  • Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and season with salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to medium low and cook, stirring frequently, until soft and golden. The onions will be ready after about 10 minutes, but you could lower the heat even more and let them cook slowly the whole time the sweet potatoes are in the oven.
  • Add the garlic to the pan with the onions and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes (depending on how high your heat is) until the garlic is fragrant.
  • To assemble the stuffed sweet potatoes, flip the sweet potatoes over so they are cut side up. Use a fork to mash the inside of the sweet potatoes a little bit, then fill each one with ¼ cup vegetarian beef and ¼ cup shredded cheddar cheese. Evenly divide the onions and avocados over the top and drizzle with cashew dressing. Garnish with minced parsley if desired.

Notes

Notes

  • You can use store bought vegetarian ground beef crumbles, but I like to keep my big batch vegetarian ground beef on hand in the freezer for recipes like this.
  • If making the vegetarian ground beef fresh for this recipe, you can reduce the oven temperature to 375ºF to cook the sweet potatoes and "beef" at the same time, allowing a little more time for the sweet potatoes to cook if needed.
  • Be sure to check out my post about creamy cashew dressing for all my tips and tricks, but I'll include this recipe here for your convenience. I often double this recipe because it's so good on everything!

Cashew Dressing

  • ¼ cup cashew butter
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 2 tablespoons lemon juice
  • 2 teaspoons honey
  • 2 teaspoons sriracha
  • 2 cloves garlic, pressed, grated, or minced
  • Coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • Cold water
  1. In a small bowl, whisk together all ingredients except the water until smooth. Taste and adjust the seasonings, and add water 1 tablespoon at a time until it is the consistency you prefer. Transfer to a mason jar and store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
